es: Reconocer frases para ganar tiempo al responder y distinguir su registro (informal, neutro o formal), el momento en que se usan y la impresión que causan.

usesVocabulary: off the top of my head

teaching.en: That's a tricky question; saying so is a neat way to buy time without sounding lost.
teaching.es: Es una pregunta complicada; decirlo es una forma hábil de ganar tiempo sin parecer perdido.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro neutro: valoras la pregunta y ganas unos segundos.

teaching.en: Offhand, I would say about twenty, although I would prefer to check before giving you an exact figure.
teaching.es: Así, de improviso, diría que unos veinte, aunque prefiero comprobarlo antes de darte una cifra exacta.
teaching.explanationEs: Offhand avisa de que das un dato aproximado, sin haberlo comprobado.

teaching.en: Off the top of my head, I cannot recall the exact date, honestly, but I can confirm it by tomorrow.
teaching.es: De memoria, no recuerdo la fecha exacta, sinceramente, pero puedo confirmarla mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Off the top of my head introduce un dato de memoria; honestly suaviza una duda.

teaching.en: Hang on, let me gather my thoughts is natural among colleagues, but it would sound abrupt in front of an interview panel.
teaching.es: «Espera, déjame ordenar mis ideas» es natural entre compañeros, pero sonaría brusco ante un tribunal de entrevista.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro informal: hang on entre amigos o compañeros, nunca ante un comité.

teaching.en: In formal settings, say allow me a moment to consider that; a considered response earns more respect than a rushed one.
teaching.es: En contextos formales, di «permítame un momento para considerarlo»; una respuesta meditada merece más respeto que una apresurada.
teaching.explanationEs: Registro formal: adecuado en entrevistas, reuniones o presentaciones.

teaching.en: When caught off guard, take a short pause, or think out loud to show the listener how you reach an answer.
teaching.es: Cuando te toman desprevenido, haz una pausa breve o piensa en voz alta para mostrar cómo llegas a una respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pausa corta suena más natural que un relleno largo; pensar en voz alta muestra tu razonamiento.
segments: When caught off guard, take a short pause, or think out
loud to show the listener how you reach an answer.

origin.text: The panel has asked about the budget. “That is a ___ question; let me think for a second before I answer.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta gana tiempo con el registro más adecuado?

choices.text: That is a demanding question; may I consider it for a moment?
Hang on a second, let me think about that for a bit.
No idea, honestly; could we please move on to the next question?

feedback.es: En un contexto formal, valorar la pregunta y pedir un momento con cortesía es lo adecuado; las otras suenan coloquiales o abandonan la respuesta.

hint.es: Piensa en el tribunal: busca la opción cortés y sin abreviaturas ni coloquialismos.

origin.text: The panel chair has just asked you, without any warning, how you would run the whole department. Everybody is waiting quietly for your reply.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué hace Laura y por qué.

choices.text: She refuses to give any number until the report is ready.
She gives a rough number and offers to check it.
She gives an exact number to close the question quickly.

feedback.es: «Off the top of her head» avisa de una cifra de memoria y «preferred to confirm it» muestra que la ofrece como aproximada, no como dato exacto.

origin.audio: Halfway through the meeting, the director asked Laura how many clients had left last year. She smiled, said that it was a tricky one, and added that, off the top of her head, she would say about forty, though she preferred to confirm it before the figures went into the report.

prompt.es: Escucha el programa y elige qué consejo final da la experta.

choices.text: Use the most formal phrase available, since politeness covers any length of pause.
Acknowledge that the question is hard, then reason aloud so the pause has content.
Rely on the informal phrase, since listeners forgive casual wording more than silence.
Fill every pause with short fillers, because silence always sounds like anxiety.

feedback.es: La experta recomienda combinar dos recursos: decir que la pregunta es difícil y pensar en voz alta, porque el oyente perdona una pausa antes que una respuesta vacía.

origin.audio: On the show, a speaking coach described three ways to buy time and ranked them by register. Hang on, she said, works among friends but sounds curt in a formal meeting. That's a tricky question is neutral, and useful because it flatters the questioner while you think. Allow me a moment to consider that is the most formal, yet it carries a risk: if the pause that follows is too long, politeness turns into anxiety. Her advice was to combine two of them, naming the difficulty and then thinking out loud, because listeners forgive a pause far more easily than they forgive an empty reply.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la coordinadora sobre el candidato?

choices.text: That the speed of his reply counted in his favour, since it showed confidence.
That the question was unfair, since nobody could have answered it well.
That the speed of his reply counted against him, since it hid how he reasons.
That the panel would have preferred a long silence to any spoken answer.

feedback.es: La coordinadora lamenta que, al responder al instante, no dejó ver cómo razona; su rapidez jugó en su contra, y no se cuestiona la pregunta ni se pide un silencio largo.

origin.text: Thanks for sitting in on the last interview. The candidate answered the surprise question at once, before the chair had finished speaking, and the answer was careless. Two seconds of silence would have told us how he reasons, which is exactly what we were hoping to assess. Instead, three panel members wrote the same comment in their notes: no sign of judgement.

prompt.es: Completa: «De memoria no puedo darte una cifra exacta, pero puedo averiguarla.»

feedback.es: Off the top of my head significa «de memoria», sin comprobar; aquí se completa con head.

origin.text: I am afraid I cannot give you an exact figure off the top of my ___. I will find it and send it to you tomorrow.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué se mostró descontento el profesor durante el simulacro?

choices.text: Because her pause was longer than a serious interview could bear.
Because she had not thought about the question before the mock interview.
Because her answer contradicted what she had said earlier in the session.
Because her phrase belonged to a more relaxed setting than the one she was in.

feedback.es: El profesor no critica la pausa ni el contenido: dice que esas mismas palabras irían bien con amigos, pero en esa sala sonaban como las de un compañero de clase.

origin.text: Notes from the mock interview: when asked about her main weakness, Anna said, “Hang on, let me gather my thoughts,” and then counted quietly to five. The senior lecturer looked unhappy. Afterwards he remarked that the same words would have passed without comment over coffee, but that in that room they sounded like a student talking to a classmate, and the rest of her answer never quite recovered its confidence.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Permítame un momento para considerar esa pregunta con calma.»

answer.text: Allow me a moment to consider that question carefully

feedback.es: Allow me a moment to consider… es la fórmula formal para pedir tiempo; carefully cierra la petición.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si te toman desprevenido, una pausa breve funciona mejor.»

feedback.es: Caught off guard significa tomado desprevenido; ahí una pausa breve resulta más creíble que las muletillas.

origin.text: The director's question was completely unexpected. When you are caught ___ guard, a short pause usually works better than a row of filler words.
